normalization_decisions.rule: Per-disaster Wikipedia article title or its disambiguated form, with article-redirect normalization where the canonical title differs from the search-form name. 15 unique values. The rule is NOT pure verbatim-article-title because some articles use redirects + lowercase variants — staged form normalizes to the article's display title where stable. Notable conventions: '1975 Banqiao Dam failure' uses article year prefix; '2020 Beirut explosion' uses article year prefix; 'AZF (factory)' uses article parenthetical disambiguator; 'Halifax Explosion' (capital E per article title); 'Senghenydd colliery disaster' (lowercase 'colliery disaster' per article title — cycle-2 fix corrected from cycle-0's capitalized form); 'Deepwater Horizon explosion' (lowercase 'explosion'); 'Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster' (per Wikipedia article title; redirects to 'Fukushima nuclear accident'); 'Benxihu Colliery disaster' (cycle-2 note: staged form uses 'Benxihu Colliery disaster' for the 1942 disaster event; underlying Wikipedia article title is just 'Benxihu Colliery' with the 1942 disaster as a section therein — staged form preserves the disaster-specific framing rather than the colliery-page title). Special-character preservation: 'Courrières' grave accent + acute accent; 'Ōkuma' macron; 'Tōhoku' macron. The audit-cycle-2 HYGIENE finding noted cycle-0's overclaim of 'verbatim article title' — the rule is more accurately article-title-with-normalization-for-redirects-and-disaster-event-framing.

Integer year (CE). Start year for multi-month/multi-day events (Deepwater Horizon Apr 20 - Jul 15 2010 → 2010; Fukushima Mar 11 2011 + ongoing → 2011; Banqiao Aug 1975 → 1975). Range: 1906 (Courrières) to 2020 (Beirut).

Comma-delimited 'City, Region/State, Country' format. Special cases: 'Benxi, Liaoning, China (then Manchukuo)' for 1942 (preserves Manchukuo political context); 'Pripyat, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union' for 1986 (preserves USSR context); 'North Sea, United Kingdom sector' for Piper Alpha (offshore); 'Gulf of Mexico, off Louisiana, United States' for Deepwater Horizon (offshore); 'Port of Beirut, Lebanon' for 2020 Beirut. Diacritic preservation: 'Courrières', 'Ōkuma'. CSV-quoted because cells contain commas.

Closed 6-value curator-normalized vocab: Mining, Chemical, Munitions/Explosives, Nuclear, Petroleum/Energy, Hydroelectric. Distribution: Mining 5 / Chemical 3 / Munitions-Explosives 2 / Nuclear 2 / Petroleum-Energy 2 / Hydroelectric 1. Classification rules: ammonium nitrate at fertilizer plant (AZF Toulouse + Texas City) = Chemical (industrial-use chemical); ammonium nitrate stockpile detonation (2020 Beirut) + ship-collision-igniting-munitions-cargo (Halifax) = Munitions/Explosives (storage/transport of explosive materials). Master's broader Energy section subdivided into Nuclear / Petroleum-Energy / Hydroelectric for benchmark granularity.

Open text source-grounded from per-disaster Wikipedia article infobox/lede causality description. Examples: 'Coal dust explosion' (Courrières); 'Methyl isocyanate gas leak from Union Carbide pesticide plant' (Bhopal); 'Reactor design flaw and operator error during safety test' (Chernobyl); '2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami disabling reactor cooling' (Fukushima); 'Wellhead blowout and gas explosion' (Deepwater Horizon); 'Ship collision detonating munitions cargo' (Halifax); 'Detonation of stockpiled ammonium nitrate' (2020 Beirut).

Categorical text source-verbatim per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 + cycle-2 source-priority rule (per-disaster infobox > lede > master bullet). Preserves source nuance (official / claimed / estimated / immediate / long-term / 'suspected' / 'confirmed' qualifiers). Post-cycle-2 examples (infobox-grounded): 'At least 3,787 officially; over 16,000 claimed' (Bhopal); '26,000–240,000' (Banqiao infobox range-verbatim); '31 direct; estimates 4,000 to several hundred thousand long-term' (Chernobyl); '1 suspected from radiation (lung cancer, 4 years later)' (Fukushima infobox Deaths field); '1,782 (confirmed)' (Halifax infobox); '218; over 7,000 injured' (2020 Beirut); '362 killed' (Monongah infobox); '437 dead and unknown number of mules' (Coalbrook infobox); '439 coal miners and a rescuer' (Senghenydd lede). CSV-quoted because cells often contain commas + semicolons + range characters.

open_questions.question: Should the staged universe include closely-related industrial disasters that were not in the curator-selected 15 (e.g., Mitsubishi Hōjō mine disaster 1914, Three Mile Island 1979, Buncefield 2005, Texas City refinery 2005)?
open_questions.answer: Open for future-cycle consideration. The current 15-row universe was curator-balanced across 6 industry categories with mining-heavy weighting documented as defensible per audit-cycle-1. If a future-cycle audit prefers broader universe + extends to 18-20 rows, the candidate additions would include Mitsubishi Hōjō (mining +1) and Three Mile Island (nuclear +1, INES 5 vs Chernobyl/Fukushima INES 7). The current 15-row selection balances comprehensiveness with bounded scope.

open_questions.question: Should Halifax Explosion be classified as Munitions/Explosives or as Maritime/Transport?
open_questions.answer: Halifax Explosion 1917 was caused by a collision between SS Mont-Blanc (carrying wartime munitions cargo) and SS Imo. While the proximate cause was a maritime collision, the disaster's industrial-engineering-failure character is the explosive-cargo handling/loading, hence the Munitions/Explosives classification. Audit-cycle-1 confirmed Munitions/Explosives categorization. If a future-cycle audit prefers Maritime/Transport, Halifax would shift to a new 7th category — but the cleaner 6-value vocab is preserved.

open_questions.question: For Banqiao Dam failure, should the cause be staged as Typhoon Nina (natural cause) or as engineering-failure (dam design + spillway capacity)?
open_questions.answer: Multiple factors contributed: Typhoon Nina's extreme rainfall + engineering flaws (spillway design capacity + dam-construction issues) + policy failures (water management decisions). Master's per-disaster article infobox Cause field is multi-factor verbatim: 'Typhoon Nina, engineering flaws, failures in policy'. Cycle-2 fix updated staged Cause from cycle-0's single-factor 'Typhoon Nina extreme rainfall overwhelming dam' to the infobox-verbatim multi-factor phrasing. Industry Category = Hydroelectric (the engineering-system that failed, regardless of natural-disaster trigger).
